h1: The 6 Best NAS Drives for Mac Time Machine Backup Under $700, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best NAS for Mac Time Machine: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 diskless NAS boxes from Synology, UGREEN and Asustor for Mac Time Machine backup, compared on bays, CPU and network speed.
mainKeyword: nas for mac time machine backup under $700
summary: The Synology DS225+ is the best NAS for Mac Time Machine backup for most households, with a polished DSM setup flow and hardware transcoding for media. The Asustor AS5402T is the performance pick with NVMe cache slots and dual 2.5GbE, the UGREEN DXP2800 is the creator-friendly option, and the Synology DS925+ is the long-term 4-bay choice.
intro: The line on the box that says under $700 hides the real cost of a NAS: every box in this ranking is diskless. You still have to buy the hard drives, and good NAS-rated drives can double the total. A sensible Mac backup setup is a two-bay box with two drives, which leaves a four-bay enclosure for people who know they will grow into it.

This ranking sorts six NAS enclosures by how well they suit a Mac household running Time Machine. We reviewed the listing specifications supplied, covering bays, processor, network ports and operating system, and we judged each on set-up friendliness, headroom and support lifecycle. Where a listing is quiet about something such as RAM, we say so instead of filling the gap.

products.name: Synology DS225+ Private Cloud Media Server
products.verdict: A two-bay Synology with an Intel CPU, hardware transcoding and the most polished Time Machine setup.
products.description:
The DS225+ is a diskless two-bay NAS with an Intel CPU, hardware transcoding and a native DSM flow for setting up Time Machine. It falls between $200 and $500 before drives.

It takes first place because Time Machine on a Mac is mostly a software problem, and DSM is the most refined software in this group. You create a shared folder, enable Time Machine from the file service settings and pick the NAS as your backup destination. Two bays let you mirror a pair of drives, so a single disk failure does not lose your history. Hardware transcoding is a bonus if you also stream video.

Buy it for a family Mac backup server that also serves media. Skip it if you want the fastest possible network ports.
cons: Network ports are not the fastest
products.idealFor: Mac households wanting a trouble-free backup server.

products.name: Asustor AS5402T, 2-Bay NAS
products.verdict: An Intel quad-core, 4GB of RAM, four M.2 cache slots and dual 2.5GbE ports.
products.description:
The AS5402T is a two-bay NAS with a 2.0GHz Intel quad-core CPU, 4GB of DDR4 RAM, four M.2 NVMe SSD cache slots and dual 2.5GbE network ports. It falls between $200 and $500.

It ranks second because it has the most detailed and strongest spec sheet. NVMe caching can speed up repeated access to frequently used files, and dual 2.5GbE gives you either faster links or link aggregation if your network supports it. For Time Machine, the first full backup is the slow one, and a faster network shortens it. The compromise is software: Asustor's operating system is less widely documented than Synology's DSM.

Choose it if you want headroom and speed. Skip it if you value the easiest Mac setup.
products.idealFor: Users who want speed and caching.
products.skipIf: You want the simplest Time Machine flow.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP2800 2-Bay
products.verdict: A two-bay UGREEN NAS aimed at creators who need active project storage alongside backup.
products.description:
The DXP2800 is a two-bay UGREEN NAS running UGREEN's own NAS operating system, positioned for content creator workflows. It falls between $200 and $500.

It ranks third because it targets a specific buyer: someone who edits video or photos and wants project storage on the network plus standard Time Machine backups. UGREEN is a newer name in NAS, so the software has a shorter track record and a smaller body of tutorials than Synology. The listing gives limited technical detail.

Buy it if you are a creator who wants shared project storage. Skip it if you want a long-established platform.
products.idealFor: Photographers and editors needing shared storage.

products.name: Synology 4-Bay DiskStation DS925+
products.verdict: Synology's newest 4-bay with a native Time Machine flow and the longest expected support window.
products.description:
The DS925+ is a diskless four-bay Synology, described as the current flagship with a native DSM Time Machine setup and the longest expected official support lifecycle. It is priced at $500 and up.

It ranks fourth because four bays are more than most Mac backups need, and with drives the total can pass your $700 limit. The advantage is longevity. Newer Synology hardware tends to receive software updates for longer, and four bays let you dedicate separate drives to Time Machine and to everything else.

Buy it if you plan to grow. Skip it if you only need to back up a couple of Macs.
cons: Total cost with drives is high
products.skipIf: You need only a simple Mac backup.

products.name: Synology DS425+ Private Cloud Media Server
products.verdict: A four-bay diskless Synology that lets you dedicate bays to Time Machine and to other storage.
products.description:
The DS425+ is a four-bay diskless NAS with Synology's well-documented DSM software and a native Time Machine setup flow. It is priced at $500 and up.

It ranks fifth because the DS925+ is the newer four-bay model and it matches the function while costing about the same on paper. Its strength is flexibility: with four bays you can dedicate two drives to Time Machine and two to media or files, without mixing the two.

Choose it if you want separate bay groups. Skip it if the newer DS925+ is available at a similar price.
products.idealFor: People splitting backup and media storage.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP4800 Plus 4-Bay
products.verdict: A four-bay UGREEN with a 5-core Intel Pentium Gold 8505, the strongest CPU here.
products.description:
The DXP4800 Plus is a four-bay UGREEN NAS with a 5-core Intel Pentium Gold 8505 processor and UGREEN's own NAS OS. It is priced at $500 and up.

It ranks last because Time Machine does not need a strong processor, so the CPU is only a benefit if you also run virtual machines, media servers and containers at once. The software is newer than Synology's, and the cost with drives is the highest in the group.

Buy it if you run many services on one box. Skip it if you mainly want Mac backups.

whatMatters.detail: Every NAS here is sold diskless. NAS-rated hard drives can cost as much as the enclosure, so budget for two at least. Check the listing for the word diskless.
Time Machine backs up over the SMB file protocol to a shared folder. A good NAS creates that share, limits its size and handles the macOS handshake. Look for Time Machine named in the feature list.
A two-bay mirror protects against a failed disk, but it does not protect against deletion, theft or a fire. Keep an offsite copy of what matters. Treat the NAS as one copy, not the only one.
Gigabit is plenty for steady daily backups. A 2.5GbE port speeds up the first full backup and large file transfers. Only the Asustor lists dual 2.5GbE in this ranking.
A NAS is a long-term appliance, so support matters. Established platforms tend to be updated for longer. Check the maker's support policy before you commit.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Family of Macs Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Per-user Time Machine quotas, RAID mirroring and a simple app. Each Mac should have its own share so backups do not fill the disk.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Synology DS225+ with two NAS drives is the easiest, while the DS925+ suits a larger household.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want four bays, a long support window or multi-gigabit networking. The Synology DS925+ or Asustor AS5402T justify the upgrade.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You back up one or two Macs. The Synology DS225+ in the $200 to $500 range covers it.

faq.a: No. Each is a diskless enclosure, so you must add your own drives. Plan on two NAS-rated drives for a mirrored setup.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with a NAS for Time Machine?
faq.a: Leaving Time Machine unlimited. Without a quota, one Mac can fill the whole share, so set a size limit for each backup.

faq.q: Is the Synology DS225+ worth it over the Asustor AS5402T?
faq.a: For ease and Mac polish, yes. For speed and caching, the Asustor wins on paper with dual 2.5GbE and four NVMe slots.
Plan an hour. Install the drives, power on, run the web setup, create a shared folder, enable Time Machine and choose the NAS in macOS.
Update the operating system, check disk health reports and replace drives at the first warnings. Keep a second backup offsite.

faq.q: Does Time Machine work over Wi-Fi?
faq.a: It can, but the first backup is slow. Use Ethernet for the initial full backup and let Wi-Fi handle the incremental ones.

finalTake: The Synology DS225+ is the best NAS for Mac Time Machine backup under $700, thanks to its polished DSM, Intel CPU and two bays. The Asustor AS5402T is the speed pick, the UGREEN DXP2800 suits creators, and the Synology DS925+ is the choice for long-term growth. Add the cost of drives to your budget before you buy.
